aboutness.notes: Whole-bundle aboutness covers eleven unique originals and one duplicate Slack attachment occurrence. The source combines a 150-day Spanish phonics and word-study sequence, ten five-lesson readers-theater scripts, and seven captured three-week reading-workshop unit guides. All 305 supported daily lessons are indexed in Layer 5. Individual model texts, shared readings, poems, and scripts remain attached to the exact lessons where they are used.

layer1_philosophy.methodology: Integrated kindergarten Spanish literacy with explicit phonological awareness and phonics, shared and independent reading, content-rich interactive read-aloud, repeated reading, readers theater, formative observation, and cumulative review
principles: Teach Spanish sound-to-print correspondences explicitly, then apply them immediately in syllables, words, shared texts, independent decodable texts, dictation, and writing.
Use recurring five-day structures, but keep the modules flexible so the parent can adjust sequence, grouping, rereading, and support to the child.
Build comprehension and knowledge through three-week content units that join model read-alouds, shared reading, poetry, minilessons, independent practice, observation, and reflection.
Use a five-day readers-theater cycle to move from meaning and prediction into shared reading, role practice, rehearsal, performance, and reflection.
Spiral-review earlier correspondences and use formative and cumulative evidence to choose the next scaffold without turning one score into a verdict on a child.
Ground abstract literacy work in family, school, technology, living things, stories, celebrations, weather, needs and wants, and motion.

layer1_philosophy.learningTheory: explicit gradual release with systematic sound-to-print teaching, syllable and word construction, repeated reading, connected-text transfer, content-rich discussion, performance, cumulative review, and observation-informed differentiation
layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: Daily observation during phonological-awareness, phonics, shared-reading, independent-reading, writing, discussion, and rehearsal work; weekly review and cumulative phonics checks; reading-workshop formative observation; and performance reflection. Evidence changes support and pacing, not the child's worth or identity.
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: Act as teacher, reading partner, and responsive observer. Model the target briefly, guide sound and text work, listen during rereading, convert classroom partner or small-group turns into parent-child or sibling dialogue, record what transferred, and choose whether to repeat, simplify, or extend the next lesson.

knowledgeBankMatches.note: The active Benchmark method covers explicit correspondence teaching, connected reading and writing, sorting, dictation, cumulative review, and assessment. Grade K applies the same method to Spanish alphabetic and syllabic foundations rather than Grade 3 morphology and multisyllabic patterns.

The active content-rich workshop method covers thematic model texts, minilessons, guided practice, independent transfer, vocabulary, observation, and synthesis. The Grade K source adds shared reading, poetry, early print concepts, and shorter independent-reading intervals.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark Grade K integrated Spanish literacy format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A coordinated Grade K Spanish program with 150 phonics and word-study days, three-week content-rich reading-workshop units, and ten five-day readers-theater sequences.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Coordinate three instructional lanes. In the 30-week phonics lane, teach one Spanish letter, digraph, contextual spelling, or review set through sound isolation, syllable and word building, shared reading, connected text, independent decodable reading, writing, and a weekly cumulative check. In each three-week reading-workshop unit, use weekly model read-alouds, two shared readings, a recurring poem, brief minilessons, independent or guided practice, observation, and reflection around one essential question. Use one five-day readers-theater sequence per content unit: introduce and predict, read together for meaning and fluency, assign roles and reread, rehearse with expression, then perform and reflect. Adapt classroom grouping into parent-child, sibling, or invited-peer turns while preserving the instructional purpose.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark five-day readers-theater format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A 20 to 25 minute daily sequence that develops comprehension, oral reading fluency, prosody, collaboration, and reflection through one script across five lessons.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Day 1 introduces the script, builds background knowledge, and invites predictions. Day 2 uses shared and choral reading to establish meaning, print concepts, and fluency. Day 3 rereads orally, discusses meaning, and assigns roles. Day 4 rehearses with attention to accuracy, rate, expression, and staging. Day 5 performs for an attentive audience, observes fluency and prosody, reflects, and extends the script's meaning. Use an original or rights-cleared script, keep every role readable and purposeful, and adapt the audience and cast to the people available at home.

layer3_structure.cadence: Three synchronized lanes: 150 phonics and word-study days across ten three-week units; 50 readers-theater lessons across ten five-day scripts; and 105 captured reading-workshop minilessons across seven three-week unit guides. These are overlapping components of a Grade K literacy block, not 305 consecutive school days.

evidence: Lectura interactiva en voz alta (10-15 min.)

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: Phonics Days 1 and 2 introduce and apply the weekly correspondence in shared reading; Day 3 transfers it into independent decodable text; Day 4 rereads and writes; Day 5 reviews and assesses. Reading workshop uses a weekly model read-aloud, two days with one shared text, two days with a second shared text, and a fifth-day unit poem plus reflection. Readers theater uses one script across five days from introduction to performance.
layer3_structure.progressionModel: Systematic Spanish alphabetic progression from letter recognition and common consonants through digraphs, context-sensitive spellings, silent h, less common letters, and cumulative review, synchronized with increasingly broad literary, scientific, civic, technological, cultural, economic, weather, and motion themes.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Every phonics week rereads and assesses the current pattern while spiraling earlier correspondences. Every reading-workshop week revisits its model and shared texts for several purposes and closes with poetry and reflection. Every theater title receives repeated oral reading, rehearsal, performance, and reflection.
studyRoutines: Hear and isolate a target sound, connect it to print, build syllables and words, and read it in a shared text.
Apply the correspondence in a short independent decodable text, reread for fluency, then write about the text.
Listen to a content-rich model text, discuss an essential question, and practice one comprehension move in shared reading.
Use poetry, repeated reading, and constructive conversation to reinforce vocabulary, expression, and meaning.
Move a short script from prediction and shared reading into roles, rehearsal, performance, and reflection.
Use observation and cumulative review to decide whether to repeat, simplify, or extend the next lesson.
layer3_structure.bookAndReaderUse: The program names shared poems, independent decodable texts, model read-alouds, shared readings, recurring unit poems, and readers-theater scripts. Homa may preserve each work's instructional purpose, but must use original, licensed, public-domain, or parent-provided text rather than reproduce copyrighted source pages or scripts.
layer3_structure.homeschoolAdaptation: Run the three lanes as components of one literacy block at a pace the child can sustain. Whole group becomes parent and child; partner reading becomes parent-child, sibling, or invited-peer reading; small group becomes one-to-one guided practice; theater roles may be doubled, narrated, or shared. Preserve the target and evidence while the parent controls timing, repetition, and stopping.

activityTypes.description: Isolate a Spanish phoneme, select its grapheme or grapheme pattern, and build CV syllables and words.
Show one Spanish letter, digraph, or contextual spelling with examples and a small contrast set.
Practice a small weekly set of frequent Spanish words in connected reading and writing.
Read a short text controlled for the current pattern, then answer or write about it.
Reread a familiar short text for accuracy, rate, phrasing, and expression.
Write syllables, words, dictated items, and a compact response connected to the reading.
Build content knowledge and model comprehension through read-aloud, shared text, and discussion.
Use a short essential or text-dependent prompt to check understanding and support discussion.
Create a readable multi-role script for repeated oral reading, rehearsal, performance, and reflection.
Extend a three-week theme through questions, source gathering, making, and a small presentation.
Record strategy use, decoding, fluency, comprehension, independence, and needed support without inventing a verdict.
